channel.title: Field Notes — Ashutosh Upadhyay
channel.description: Notes on cloud platform engineering, GitOps, and agentic infrastructure for pharmaceutical R&D — what actually works.

item.title: EKS or Managed Agent Runtime? A Framework for the Decision You'll Face Twice
item.description: The migration looked straightforward. Then we found five categories of blockers. Here's the framework we wish we'd had before we started.

item.title: Multi-Tenant FinOps: The Three Silent Bugs That Made Our AWS Cost Data Untrustworthy
item.description: We built the join, ran it, got 1.8% coverage. It looked like a data problem. It was a .lower() call — and two more silent bugs followed.

item.title: GPU Digital Pathology AI on Kubernetes: What KEDA ScaledJobs Actually Do Under Load
item.description: Burst GPU workloads, silent Karpenter version traps, and why your SQS consumer should never be a ScaledJob.

item.title: Ingesting 129 GB for an AI Agent: Five Design Mistakes Caught Before Build
item.description: We had a design. The advisor caught five blockers before a single line was written. Here's what changed and why it mattered.

item.title: Closing the Feedback Loop: How User Corrections Become Domain Knowledge
item.description: The agent was wrong. The user corrected it. The next user got the same wrong answer. Here's how to close the loop — without fine-tuning.

item.title: Cross-Session Agent Memory: What Persists, What Shouldn't, and Why It's Hard
item.description: Every session starts cold. Users re-teach the same preferences. Here's how to give your agent real memory without creating a privacy disaster.

item.title: Observability for AI Agents: Beyond Langfuse Traces
item.description: Langfuse catches bad tool data. Prometheus catches the stuck pod. CloudWatch catches the $12 session. Here's how three layers work together — and where each one falls short alone.

item.title: Teaching an Agent to Think Like a Domain Expert — Without Fine-Tuning
item.description: Not fine-tuning. Not prompt-stuffing. A skills system that retrieves domain heuristics at query time — and the failure modes that shaped it.

item.title: Releasing an AI System Is Not Like Releasing Software
item.description: A tag-only image bump left the UI, presentation, and diagrams five versions stale. None of it errored. Here's what a real AI system release checklist looks like.

item.title: Your Agent Is Only As Good As Its Data Pipeline
item.description: The agent gets the credit. The data pipeline does the work. Here's the production ingestion architecture that keeps a 19-source research agent reliable.

item.title: Managed Agent Runtimes: Read the Fine Print
item.description: I run agents on Kubernetes and evaluated moving them to a managed agent platform. Here's what genuinely improves, what quietly becomes your problem, and why a hybrid split was the honest answer.

item.title: Your Agent Is a Confused Deputy
item.description: Security lessons from putting an autonomous, tool-calling agent in front of regulated enterprise data — including a cross-tenant vulnerability I shipped, found, and closed.

item.title: Every Public Benchmark Is Useless to You
item.description: Building a standing internal evaluation suite — and the four ways my harness broke before it produced a single trustworthy number.

item.title: What Your AI Agent Actually Costs
item.description: Your invoice tells you the total. It never tells you who spent it, which tokens were wasted, or whether the last model upgrade paid for itself.

item.title: Multi-Agent AI Collaboration
item.description: Why one agent isn't enough — and how to build a team of AI specialists that research, analyze, synthesize, and critique each other's work, with full observability via Langfuse.

item.title: From Chatbot to Autonomous Research System
item.description: How I built a 33-tool AI agent that autonomously queries databases, builds knowledge graphs, and generates research reports — running on Kubernetes.

item.title: Building AI With AI on Claude Code
item.description: How I use Claude Code's agent system to build AI systems — with a mandatory Advisor that catches production bugs, persistent memory that compounds across sessions, and a full EKS deployment architecture.
